While reviewing the text, noticed that unified approach not always followed for commonly used abbreviations...
For example:
in [10.1.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v101-generic-oauth-and-oidc-security)
> ... This requires that client-generated secrets, such as the **proof key for code exchange (PKCE)** 'code_verifier', ...

but right after this in [10.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v102-oauth-client)
> ... or a frontend **Single Page Application (SPA**, aka browser-based application).

or another example right in one sentence in [10.4.12](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v104-oauth-authorization-server)
>  Verify that for a given client, the authorization server only allows the 'response_mode' value that this client needs to use. For example, by having the authorization server validate this value against the expected values or by using **pushed authorization request (PAR)** or **JWT-secured Authorization Request (JAR)**.

Could it be more convenient if for all commonly used abbreviations the words will be always started from Capital letter and abbreviation will be putted in brackets? For example: Pushed Authorization Request (PAR).
And check that such abbreviations are putted into Appendix A Glossary. 

And there are some other examples through the text for:
- cross-site request forgery (CSRF) in [3.3.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x12-V3-Web-Frontend-Security.md#v33-cookie-setup)  
- local or remote file inclusion (LFI, RFI), and server-side request forgery (SSRF) in [5.3.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x14-V5-File-Handling.md#v53-file-storage)
-  time-based, one-time passwords (TOTPs) in [6.5.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x15-V6-Authentication.md#v65-general-multi-factor-authentication-requirements), [6.5.5](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x15-V6-Authentication.md#v65-general-multi-factor-authentication-requirements)
- cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) in [7.2.4](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x16-V7-Session-Management.md#v72-fundamental-session-management-security), [11.5.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x20-V11-Cryptography.md#v115-random-values)
- insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA) in [8.2.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x17-V8-Authorization.md#v82-general-authorization-design)
- broken object property level authorization (BOPLA) in [8.2.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x17-V8-Authorization.md#v82-general-authorization-design)
- proof key for code exchange (PKCE) in [10.1.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v101-generic-oauth-and-oidc-security), [10.2.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v102-oauth-client), [10.4.6](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v104-oauth-authorization-server) 
- cross-site request forgery (CSRF) in [10.2.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v102-oauth-client)
- pushed authorization requests (PAR) in [10.4.12](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v104-oauth-authorization-server), [10.4.13](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v104-oauth-authorization-server) 

And one more similar point: 
Should we use ZIP instead of zip in [2.1.2](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x11-V2-Validation-Business-Logic.md#v21-validation-and-business-documentation)? There is style correction to do for us, one way or another (to camel-case or to lower case). Please see #1875

> Could it be more convenient if for all commonly used abbreviations the words will be always started from Capital letter and abbreviation will be putted in brackets? For example: Pushed Authorization Request (PAR).

The short answer is no. See the links in this comments: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1875#issuecomment-1963898816


> ... pushed authorization request (PAR)

One of the reason why we use it like this is that the specification for PAR uses it that way https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9126.html

So we need (to pick) our styleguide first...
